findings.title: zip(error_ids, events.values()) misaligns when nodestore returns fewer results
findings.body: In fetch_error_details, `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` returns a dict that may omit keys for missing events. The code then does `zip(error_ids, events.values())`, which pairs error_ids positionally with whatever values the dict contains. If any event_id is not found in nodestore, the dict will have fewer entries than error_ids, causing subsequent event_ids to be paired with the wrong event data. For example, with error_ids=[a,b,c] and only a,c found, the zip produces (a,data_a) and (b,data_c), attributing c's data to b. The fix is to iterate over node_ids and look up each in the returned dict, e.g. `for node_id, event_id in zip(node_ids, error_ids): data = events.get(node_id)`.

findings.title: Falsy check on age/timestamp allows both fields when age=0
findings.body: validate_timestamp uses `if self.initial_data.get("age")` and validate_age uses `if self.initial_data.get("timestamp")`. Since `age` is an IntegerField with no min_value, a value of 0 is valid but falsy. If a report contains both `"age": 0` and `"timestamp": 123`, the `self.initial_data.get("age")` check returns 0 (falsy), so the mutual-exclusion validation is silently skipped and both fields are accepted. The check should use `"age" in self.initial_data` or `self.initial_data.get("age") is not None` instead.

findings.title: update() reads 'detector_type' key but serializer field is named 'type', so type can never be updated
findings.body: In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the code does `validated_data.get("detector_type", instance.group_type)`. However, the serializer field is declared as `type = serializers.CharField()` and `validate_type` returns a GroupType, so the validated_data dict will contain the key `"type"`, not `"detector_type"`. This means the `.get("detector_type", ...)` always falls back to `instance.group_type`, making it impossible to update the detector type via PUT. The key should be `"type"` to match the serializer field name.

findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with hardcoded empty data instead of actual query results
findings.body: When the `use-table-widget-visualization` feature flag is enabled, the code renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />`, completely ignoring the actual `result.data`, `result.meta`, `fields`, and other props that are available in scope. This means enabling the feature flag will show empty tables in all dashboard widget cards instead of real data. The actual data from `result` should be passed to the component.

findings.title: get_recommended_event() called per issue in PR comment generation may be expensive
findings.body: get_environment_info calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for each issue (up to 5) when generating a merged PR comment. get_recommended_event typically involves a nodestore fetch or event lookup. This happens synchronously during comment body construction, adding latency to the PR comment workflow. Consider caching or batching these lookups, or making environment info best-effort with a timeout.

findings.title: Typo 'segements' in comment
findings.body: The comment on line 88 reads 'If no segments were ingested then we can skip deleting the segements.' — 'segements' should be 'segments'.

findings.title: Analytics event recorded before feature flag check, may record events for disabled orgs
findings.body: analytics.record('preprod_artifact.api.assemble', ...) is called unconditionally before the `features.has('organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble', ...)` check. This means every request to this endpoint generates an analytics event even when the feature is disabled and the request will return 404. If this is not intentional, the analytics call should be moved after the feature flag check.

findings.title: Data migrations gutted to no-ops with reference to migration 0921 not present in this PR
findings.body: Both migrations 0917 and 0920 are changed to no-ops with a comment referencing '0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py', but that migration is not included in this PR. The test for migration 0917 is also removed. If migration 0921 does not already exist in the codebase, the saved-search-to-views data conversion is effectively lost. Ensure 0921 exists and has its own test coverage before merging.
